learning_outcomes.text: The student will be able to handle coordinate systems in 2 and 3-dimensional elements
The student will acquire the knowledge to identify the degrees of freedom of a multibody system
The student will be able to apply the analytical tools necessary for the kinematic and dynamic analysis of multibody systems
The student will be able to solve problems of kinematics and dynamics of multibody systems
The student will be able to manipulate computational tools for the dynamic simulation of mechanical elements
The student will be able to model different mechanical systems with n degrees of freedom
The student will be able to interpret the mechanical behavior of multibody systems

assessment_methods.method: Written exam for kinematics and dynamics of multibody systems units
Written exam for the mechanical vibrations unit

assessment_rules: The weighted average of the three parts must be greater than or equal to 5. To pass the course, a minimum of 2 points out of 5 is required in the kinematics and dynamics exam, and a minimum of 1 point out of 3 in the vibrations exam. These minimum scoring criteria apply to both continuous assessment and assessment during the final exam for ordinary and extraordinary calls.
